hook: SCP-2598, the Traveling Moth Salesman, is a moth in a tiny helmet that talks to people by bumping into their heads in Morse code, and all it really wants is to sell you a helmet. It is a short comedy piece, and nearly all of the fun lives in the interview.
whyItMatters:
It shows how far a single joke can go when the delivery is right. The clinical setup, with mandatory Morse training and a lead researcher picked for his fluency in code, plays completely straight against an infomercial that never stops.

It also represents the gentlest end of the Safe class: a harmless object whose containment mostly comes down to food, a lamp and patience.
thingsToNotice: Every reply is written in capitals without punctuation, which suits a transcript of tapped code and also reads like a shouted TV ad. Asked where it came from, the moth turns the question into a conversion story, then slides into installment pricing, child safety and stocking-stuffer pitches. Its one moment of hesitation, twenty seconds spent circling the light after being told no human could wear the helmet, is the best beat in the piece, and its comeback about moth friends lands perfectly. The footnote saying the hanging light was installed at its own request is a last small joke.
